Shakti Peetha of Devi (Mata Sati's ringlet)
Patal Devi (cave shrine - King Kansa's deity)

history.dynasty: Legendary antiquity (mythology); the present structure is described as largely 18th century (per srimandir.com - verify)
history.summary: The famous Shiva shrine of Mathura, revered as the city's protector - Bhuteshwar means 'Lord of all beings' and the temple is the Kotwal (guardian) of Mathura, believed to shield the city from evil forces; it is said to stand on Bhuteshwar Tila and to date from the founding of Mathura itself. One of the few Mathura temples not dedicated to Krishna, it houses a swayambhu Shivalinga constantly bathed with milk, water and bilva leaves. It is also counted as a Shakti Peetha, where the ringlet of Mata Sati fell. The Patal Devi cave within the campus houses the deity worshipped by King Kansa. Mythology: Mathura was founded when Sri Ram's younger brother Shatrughan slew the demon Madhu (Lavanasura), and the temple's establishment is linked to that age; a Skanda Purana legend says Shiva took the form of Bhuteshwar to guard Mathura after Krishna left Earth (weakly sourced - verify), and devotional lore holds that Krishna himself worshipped Shiva here. One travel source claims an ancient shrine mentioned in Buddhist-era texts and flourishing under the Guptas, with a rebuild in 1670 and management by the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Trust from 1951 (all weakly sourced - verify). NOTE: the popular 'oldest temple in Mathura' claim is devotional tradition, not archaeologically dated; the Shakti Peetha ringlet legend also has a variant placing a different body part at Mathura - verify. Opening-hour conflict: 5:00 AM-1:00 PM and 4:30-10:30 PM versus 5:00 AM-12:00 PM and 4:00-9:00 PM in different sources (flagged - verify).

name: Bhuteshwar Mahadev Temple
town_description: Mathura is an ancient city on the banks of the Yamuna in the Braj region, revered as the birthplace of Lord Krishna and counted among Hinduism's Sapta Puri (seven holy cities). A major pilgrimage centre for millennia, it is dotted with temples, ghats and kunds, and lies about 160 km south-east of Delhi on the Delhi-Agra corridor.

travel.airport: Kheria Airport, Agra, about 46-60 km from Mathura; Indira Gandhi International Airport, Delhi, about 160 km.
travel.railway: Mathura Junction, about 1-2 km from the temple (per brajbhoomitourandtravels); auto-rickshaws and taxis available.
travel.road: At Bhuteshwar Tila / Bhuteshwar Crossroad, Krishna Nagar, Mathura 281004 - central Mathura, near Krishna Janmabhoomi and Dwarkadhish Temple; about 4 km from the city centre.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Sawan (July-August) and Maha Shivratri are the peak devotional periods with huge crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Sources conflict: 5:00 AM-1:00 PM and 4:30-10:30 PM versus 5:00 AM-12:00 PM and 4:00-9:00 PM - verify locally before travel. No entry fee.
